column1: # Trust and merge invariant rows. Tab-separated, one line per row (or row arm, as ROW:arm).
# Read by tests/common/rows.rs (row state), tests/invariants.rs (table checks) and tests/mutants/run.sh (mutants).
# state: enforced (holds; mutant is a patch that must make the test fail) | control (holds; its guard has not landed, so nothing to mutate yet)
#        known-violation (murk breaks it today; the test fails once the target holds) | pending (needs behaviour that does not exist yet; runs only with MURK_ROWS=pending, never fails)
# fix: the change that flips the row, or - for an enforced row. binary: integration test file stem, or lib for a unit test.
# mutant: for an enforced row, the patch under tests/mutants/; otherwise the guard to disable once the fix lands.
# review: ids of the test-quality review findings the row also answers (comma-separated), or -.

A removal this machine accepted is permanent: replays, signatures and saves by the removed key are refused.
A merge side never brings a removed recipient back.
A save over an older revision never writes a removed recipient back.
Merging the removal into a branch the removed member wrote to keeps them out.
A removed signer's later vault is refused on a new branch: only commits at or before the removal commit get the pre-removal exception.
A replayed pre-removal vault is refused on a new branch: only commits at or before the removal commit get the pre-removal exception.
A merge whose theirs ours already descends from, over an ancestor signed by a removed member, exits 0 with ours byte for byte.

column6: drop the new result load_verdict call
column8: Consistency check: every stored merge ran the murk driver, and the merging machine and every observer accept its result as a direct save.
A member whose machine has not confirmed their own signing key merges: this machine would refuse the signed result, so the driver signs nothing and .murk stays ours, byte for byte.
A theirs whose MAC fails: .murk is ours byte for byte, the pin is unchanged, exit non-zero naming theirs.
A keyless merge driver where theirs changed only the meta exits 1 and leaves .murk unchanged.
A keyed merge whose theirs is signed outside the anchor and adds a recipient: the file stays ours, the pin unchanged.
A keyed merge whose ancestor's MAC fails: the file stays ours, the pin unchanged, stderr names the ancestor.

An input that parses but fails authentication leaves .murk equal to ours byte for byte; an input that cannot be parsed (here theirs with a byte-order mark) leaves conflict markers that never load. In both cases nothing is signed and the pin is unchanged.
Through the merge driver, a grant both sides changed is dropped; a one-sided change is taken.
A grant load refuses a vault signed by a key outside the key file's anchor, though the key is a recipient and the grant's record survived its save.
A key file naming an age signer without a verifying key never verifies a vault, even when the vault registers that key.

column8: An expired, revoked grant key re-authorized as a recipient is refused by circle authorize and on load; today it reads as an operator.
A pinless runner refuses a vault listing a revoked grant key, by the vault's own revoked_grants.

column8: A signer's save after murk trust of a pre-grant revision keeps the revoked grant key in revoked_grants.
A vault signed by a grant key is refused as one a grant key signed, not only as an untrusted signer or a listed former grant.
A grant key never signs, even after dropping its record; a trusted signature that re-lists the grant key as a plain recipient is refused too.
A non-member adding themselves to a group is refused on every other machine.
A non-member who re-creates a group a member deleted, with themselves in it, is refused by machines that saw the deletion.
Revoking a group's sole member is refused without --allow-orphan; with it the revoke reports the orphaned group and any recipient clears it.

A merge that leaves a group's values with no member who is still a recipient conflicts and names the value; the group-no-longer-exists conflict holds it, and the merge post-check also stops the merge, so the mutant disables both.
A two-way merge whose result keeps a group with values and no member who is a recipient conflicts on the group; only the merge post-check holds it.
An ssh-rsa person refuses a forged unsigned vault until murk trust, and their next write does not happen.
A mixed team: an unsigned file with the pinned id, counter +3 and an extra recipient is refused, and the next write does not happen.
An unsigned vault whose ciphertexts were swapped fails the integrity check: with no signature, the MAC is the only guard.
A replace ref that makes the removal commit an ancestor does not change which committed vault murk reads.
A graft in info/grafts or GIT_GRAFT_FILE that makes the removal commit an ancestor does not change which committed vault murk reads.
When the commit a removal was recorded at is missing, the commit checked out counts as not an ancestor of it, so a removed member's later vault is refused.
With MURK_NO_SIGNER_PIN=1 an existing pin still refuses a rolled-back file and is left unchanged.
A teammate 256 saves ahead is accepted, 257 refused as beyond the window; a lopsided merge keeps both sides' entries.
A deliberate revert by murk trust then a save is accepted by a teammate whose reference is a reverted revision.

murk verify prints a distinct lineage line for a descendant, a non-descendant and a branch with no reference.

Format-3 outcome of R-L-gitrevert: git revert of a vault commit with a later vault commit stops with a conflict on .murk, which stays byte for byte as it was, and the driver names theirs as rolled back.
A cherry-pick of a revert commit over later vault work: the same refusal as R-L-gitrevert:v3.
Stated limit: a cherry-pick of a vault commit over its genuine parent applies as git does, with the later rotation kept and the result signed by the merging key.

column6: keep the new fields in the pin file instead of the sidecar
column8: A pin rewritten as murk 0.15 writes it keeps the lineage sidecar and its fields.
A pin rewritten as murk 0.15 writes it leaves the sidecar's bytes, deleted_groups and identity fields unchanged.

column6: write superseded entries without the generation filter
column8: A save after murk trust of an older revision (which lowers the counter outside git) never writes a prev entry at or above its own generation.
A legacy vault carrying a grouped value or group membership verifies only under blake3v4 and newer; every older prefix is refused.
A legacy vault carrying a grant verifies only under blake3v5 and newer; every older prefix is refused.
A legacy vault carrying a policy verifies only under blake3v6 and newer; every older prefix is refused.
A removal another worktree records between a save's decision and its publish stops the publish; the save decides again, refuses carrying the removed key, and leaves the vault file unchanged.
A removal recorded between a keyed merge's decision and its write of %A stops the write; the merge runs again, refuses the side the removed key signed, and %A keeps ours' bytes.
A trust state that changes before every publish stops the save after 3 attempts with nothing written.
Another thread can take the pin lock while a save signs: the pin lock is never held across a signature.
The publish section renames the vault and writes the sidecar and the pin under the pin lock without asking for a lock again, and releases it.
Under the pin lock, vault::lock and pins::update return the lock-order error at once instead of blocking, and write nothing.
A vault file another program changes between a save's read and its publish stops the save at once, with no restart, and leaves that program's bytes, the pin and the sidecar as they are.
A commit that moves HEAD between a save's decision and its publish makes the save decide again before it publishes.
A stale fork's genuine file that still lists a member this machine recorded as removed, numbered above the removal, is refused on load; the pin keeps the record and the next write does not happen.
A teammate's re-authorization of a removed member is refused on a machine that recorded the removal until murk trust --re-add there; the authorizing machine's own save clears its record.
A merge of a branch that re-adds a member this machine recorded as removed stops with ours and names --re-add; taking theirs with --re-add, or authorizing first, then ends clean.
A load never clears a removal record: a branch accepted before the removal still loads a vault listing the member, and the record stays for every other branch.
Stated limit: a runner with no pin, anchored only by MURK_TRUSTED_SIGNERS, has no removal record and loads a stale fork that lists a removed member.

A removal recorded before the upgrade gets its sidecar copy on the first read by this release, without a change to the pin file, so an older component that clears the pin file's record does not undo it.
Under MURK_NO_SIGNER_PIN the pin file's removal record still refuses the stale fork, and the copy on read writes neither a sidecar nor the pin.
A sidecar that cannot be written does not fail the load: murk warns once that an older component can still erase the records.
A merge result that lists a removed key is a conflict where the removal applies, even when a side above the removal lists the key; where the removal does not apply, such a side still re-adds it.
A save over a file that lists a key this machine recorded as removed is refused where the removal applies, whatever the file's generation; a save that adds the key itself is allowed.
A read copies a pin-file removal record the sidecar lacks, with the pin's vault id, and leaves the pin file; a read with nothing to copy takes no lock and writes nothing.
A record an older component clears between the unlocked read and the copy under the lock is still copied.
A pin update that writes no pin still copies a removal record the sidecar lacks, and leaves the pin file.
After an older component clears a removal record in the pin file and trusts the key again, a read lays the sidecar's copy over it: the key stays removed and untrusted.
A pin read on a thread that holds the pin lock returns the lock-order error instead of copying under a second lock.

Stored soak sequence: after a teammate re-authorizes a member this machine recorded as removed, its load is refused and names --re-add; after murk trust --re-add here it loads, and its own save lists the member.
murk trust --re-add of a recorded key the vault does not list clears this machine's record and writes nothing, so a later re-authorization loads here.

A forged ancestor that lists a removed member never exempts a side that re-adds them: theirs is refused and .murk stays ours; over an authority ancestor that lists them, the side passes and the recipient merge stops.

After an older component clears the pin file's removal record, the sidecar copy this release wrote on the revoke still refuses the stale fork, with a message that names an older murk component and --re-add.
Stated limit: a removal an older component records and clears before this release reads the pin has no copy, so this release loads the stale fork.

Release checklist, stated limit: an older component under the same HOME loads the stale fork and saves a vault the removed member reads; the sidecar is untouched and this release then refuses the vault. Ignored unless MURK_OLDER_BIN names a murk 0.15.x binary.
Stated limit: a runner that keeps its HOME but loads only with MURK_TRUSTED_SIGNERS records no removal and loads the stale fork.

Stated limit: the merge driver judges by the pin under the HOME git gives it; with no pin no input is trusted and .murk stays ours, with another HOME's older pin there is no removal record; every arm stops and signs nothing.

The sidecar is written before the pin file: a write that fails between them leaves a new record in force and a cleared record in the pin file, which the next read copies back and the next write mirrors.
A sidecar whose vault id differs from the pin's is dropped, so the vault an older component accepted at this path is judged with no record of the old vault's removals.
With the pin file gone, its sidecar's removal records still apply to the vault of its id, with no trust decision, and to no other vault.
